Jackson Core Shaded Code
================================================================================

Schubfach number-writing code. The upstream Jackson Core JAR retains the three
corresponding license files under META-INF; the GridGrind fat JAR retains those
files unchanged and reproduces their material terms here so `--license` exposes
the complete legal surface.

Jackson Core's upstream NOTICE identifies the FastDoubleParser attribution as
"Copyright © 2023 Werner Randelshofer, Switzerland. MIT License." The retained
FastDoubleParser license file carries the 2024 copyright notice reproduced
below. Both upstream statements are preserved rather than silently reconciling
their different years.

================================================================================
Container-Only Software
================================================================================

The published container image adds an Azul Zulu build of OpenJDK and operating
system/font packages that are not part of the executable GridGrind JAR. Their
licenses are not represented by a single GridGrind license expression. The
runtime preserves the base image and Debian package legal material, including
the JRE legal directory under /usr/lib/jvm and package copyright files under
/usr/share/doc. GridGrind-specific legal files are copied to
/usr/share/doc/gridgrind. Published images also carry provenance and an SBOM
attestation for the resolved image contents.

Published runtime base:
azul/zulu-openjdk:26-jre@sha256:9382c343f6de2c9f2633b7f629380f9c2a9444df8768a880c690bd5ea74f51b6

The Dockerfile pins the Azul Zulu image by manifest-list digest. Azul publishes
the base-image Dockerfiles and the Zulu licensing/source-availability materials
at:

https://github.com/zulu-openjdk/zulu-openjdk
https://docs.azul.com/core/tpl
https://www.azul.com/products/core/openjdk-terms-of-use/
https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+sources

The image's package copyright files and published SBOM identify the additional
Ubuntu and font packages. GridGrind does not relicense those components or
represent their terms as part of GridGrind's MIT license. Anyone redistributing
the aggregate image must assess and satisfy the applicable notice, source-
availability, trademark, patent, and other license conditions for that
distribution.

GridGrind does not make a separate written source-code offer for third-party
container components. Azul's published source-availability process and the
Ubuntu source archive are the identified upstream source mechanisms; this
notice does not represent that those mechanisms satisfy every commercial or
jurisdiction-specific redistribution scenario.
